FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted Lubricants and Related Products Related Products Division Council. by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum Coal and

Molybdenum disulphide in concentrated paste form is an important solid lubricant. It can be easily It has found wide application for reducing friction and metal to metal contact applied in paste form. under extreme pressure conditions, for example, in press fittings, power screws, running-in-lubricant for new parts and gears. It is applied where there are chances of gelling and welding. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

OF DROPPING

This test method covers the determination of the dropping point of lubricating grease, this point being the temperature at which the first drop of material falls from the cup. A-2 SIGNIFICANCE AND USE

The test method is useful to assist in identifying the grease as to type and for establishing and maintaining bench marks for quality control. The results are to be considered to have only limited significance with respect to service performance as dropping point is a static test. Cooperative testing indicates that, in general, dropping point by this method and test method IS 1418 [ P : 52 ] : 1971 are in agreement. In case where results differ, there is no known significance. However, agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser as to the test method used is advisable. NOTE A-3 APPARATUS

the dropping Dropping Point In general, point is the temperature at which the grease passes from a semisolid to a liquid state under the conditions of test. This change in sta.te is typical of greases containing as thickeners soaps of conventional types. Greases containing as conventional thickeners materials other than soaps may, without change in state, separate oil.

Thermometer

Immersion thermometer ( 76-mm immersion ), graduated in Celcius degrees, having a range from - 5 to 400�C and contorming to the requirements for thermometer 3C as prescribed in ASTM Specification E 1 and shown in D, Fig. 1 or its equivalent. A-3.1.5 Accessories

Thermometer clamp as shown in E-l, bushings as shown in E-2 and E-3, bushing support ring as shown in E-4, thermometer depth gauge as shown in E-5, and a metal rod as shown in E-6, and CUP gauge as shown in E-7, ail of Fig. 1. A-3.2 Ahminium Block Oven

An aluminium block oven of the design and dimensions shown in Fig. 2. The block shall be equipped with an integral cartridge-type heater. Control of the current to the heater shall be used maintain the desired oven to obtain and temperature.

A-4.3 Select and use test tubes and accessories E-l, E-2, and E-3 to minimize wobble of the thermometer. All components E-l through E 4 on the thermometer in the order shown by the thermometer assembly (F) Fig. 1. Adjust the bushing E-3 and the bushing support ring E-4 so that E-4 is about 25 mm from the tip of the thermometer. Place the cup support C in tube B. Insert the thermometer depth gauge E-5 and the thermometer assembly in the tube. Position the thermometer so that the tip bottoms in the gauge. Adjust the bushing E-2 and the thermometer clamp E-l so that the bushing shoulders on the top edge of the tube. By use of the cup gauge E-7 select for test a cup conforming to the dimensions of the gauge. Check the diameter of the bottom opening of the cup using as gauges a 2*78-mm rod as the GO gauge and a 2.83 mm rod as the No-GO gauge. If the orifice is undersize it

A-4.4 Fill the grease cup by pressing the larger opening into the grease to be tested until the cup is filled. Remove excess grease flush with the top edge of the cup with a spatula. Gently press the cup, held in a vertical position with the smaller opening at the bottom, down over the metal rod E-6, Fig. 1, until the latter protrudes about `25 mm. Press the rod against the cup in such a manner that the rod makes contact at both the upper and lower peripheries of the cup. Maintain this contact, rotating the cup in the rod along the index finger to give it a spiral-like motion down the rod to remove a conical section of the grease which adheres along the rod. As the cup approaches the end of the rod, carefully slip the rod out of the cup so that a smooth film of reproducible thickness remains inside the cup. A-4.5 Remove the thermometer assembly and depth gauge from the tube. Place the grease cup on the cup support in the test tube and carefully reinsert the thermometer assembly. Make no further adjustment as the thermometer bulb is now positioned to provide adequate clearance between the tip of the bulb and cup orifice. A-4.6 Remove an empty tube from the oven and gently insert the tube assembly, G Fig. 1, making certain that the cup remains upright in the cup support. If the cup is tilted, the thermometer bulb may come in contact with the film of grease and result in an erroneous value. A-4.7 Multiple simultaneously. A-5 A-5.1 determinations may be made

The difference between two test results obtained by the same operator with the same apparatus under constant operating conditions on identical test material would, in the long run, in the normal and correct operation of the test method, exceed the following values in only one case on twenty: Grease Dropping "C Up to 116 117 to 221 222 to 277 258 to 330 A-6.2 Reproducibility 5.5 7.7 4.4 5.5 "C

The difference between two single and independent results obtained by different operators working in different laboratories on identical test material would, in the long run, in the normal and correct operation of the test method, exceed the following values in only one case in twenty: Grease Dr@ping "C Up to 116 117 to 221 222 to 277 278 to 330 A-6.3 Bias 8.9 11.7 13.9 23-9 "C

There is no bias for this test method because the value of the dropping point can be defined only in terms of the test method.

B-2.4 Add 2-3 drops of Methyl Orange Indicator and neutralise by the dropwise addition of concentrate hydrochloric acid with constant stirring. B-Z.5 Add 30 ml of ammonium acetate solution and 10 ml glacial acetic acid and bring almost to boil. B-2.6 Add lead acetate solution slowly with constant stirring until an excess of 30 ml has been added. The bulk of the reagent should be added at a fixed rate of 30 ml in 2 minutes with mechanical stirring. Tannic acid solution is used as an external indicator, the endpoint being reached when a drop of filtrate added to a small volume of the tannic acid solution on a spot plate fails to develop a brown colouration. B-2.7 Bring the solution to almost boiling condition and allow to remain at this temperature for one hour. B-2.8 Filter the precipitate on to a 15 cm No. 42 Whatman Filter Paper and wash thoroughly with hot water. Place on hot plate and allow to fume vigorously ( do not cover the beaker ), Continue heating until the sample is white and the volume of the acid is about 5 ml. thorough!y to ensure uniform dispersion. Transfer one small drop of this diluted dispersion to a clearly microscope slide and cover with a slip ensuring even distribution of the suspension and removal of air pockets. Count the number of particles (t) in a total area (a) of the slide sufficiently large to contain at least 100 particles and consisting of at least 10 sub-areas chosen at random over the slide. G-3.2 Count the number of particles (9) greater than 5 microns in diameter in an area (6) of the slide suficiently large to contain at least 50 such particles at the same magnification. If less than 50 particles are counted when the area (b) is 100 times the area (a) the count may be discontinued. C-4 CALCULATION particles greater than 5 microns in diameter, percent
